---
title: "Meet erase restore quarantine"
description: "Reconcile the independent erase ledger before restoring service."
---

This runbook grants no restore authority. Security HOLD, GA HOLD and the ban on
wider Meet AI enablement remain. Pax owns integration; Selene reviews security;
Rex owns migration order, backups and restore admission; Cora owns hold decisions.

## Current implementation boundary

V22 is stacked on V9. `erase-reconcile.ts` implements ledger enumeration, outcome
ordering and quarantine decisions through injected ports. The migration supplies
an inert admission RPC and durable intent identities. It never releases a fence.
No cron, runtime binding, key, environment value or flag is installed.

The restore runtime adapters are still required from V12, V14, V17 and V20.
This PR does not qualify a working restore: disposable PostgreSQL and actual
channel/playground DO replay must pass AT-10(i)–(vi) and RT-O before admission.
An absent adapter leaves the meeting held. Local map-backed tests prove the
coordinator decisions, not PostgreSQL, DO cold-load or storage behavior.

## Admission and verification

1. Rex separately admits the disposable rehearsal or actual recovery. Isolate
   every restored store from serving, workers, AI jobs, checkpoints and indexes.
   Apply V4, V2, V10 and the store migrations before invoking the V22 RPC.
2. Use the independent V9 service in the isolated keyed server runtime. Its
   `verify()` must validate the complete DO and R2 chains to the same head.
   Never copy the ledger key into the restore job or meeting room Worker.
3. Rebuild holds from every retained `hold_create` and `hold_release` event,
   including events newer than the restored snapshot. Install this projection
   under the exclusive workspace hold barrier. Preserve active events for their
   lifetime and recovery window. Missing events, a pending transition, a gap,
   unavailable ledger or mirror disagreement keeps all stores quarantined.
4. Only the database owner may admit `meet_restore_quarantines` and certify its
   verified head and hold projection. The service role can invoke the admission
   RPC but cannot alter these control rows. Pass the configured protected
   workspace ids; use synthetic ids in rehearsals and never commit the real EC id.
5. Supply `ReconcilePort` adapters. `replay` recreates the plan, operation and
   progress rows by immutable operation key and dispatches the normal fenced
   worker. Each destructive batch rechecks the ledger head and shared workspace
   hold barrier, then meeting fence. External DO/storage applies require expiring
   apply leases and authenticated callbacks; never keep SQL locks across calls.
   The coordinator's head check alone cannot serialize an external apply.
6. Replay committed and no-outcome intents in sequence. A restored cancellation
   appends `aborted/cancelled` and restarts verification at the new head. An
   aborted/refused outcome may be superseded by a later committed outcome;
   cancellation followed by commitment is a protocol failure. Never replay a
   final `not_committed` key. An active hold keeps `restore_hold`; escalate a
   held no-outcome intent to Cora without deleting anything.
7. Replay transcript/notes by stable ids. For documents, use a verified post-erase
   copy or reapply the block-MAC plan to quarantined bytes. Never stamp a target
   generation onto old bytes. With no history cutoff, clear every restored
   version for that document only. Replay playground rooms without personal
   project access, label removals with locators, legacy audio rows and generated
   object paths, and each registered derived partition. Recovery copies remain
   isolated for their own reconciliation.
8. `verify` counts every store's residuals and verifies actual DO/room cold loads.
   Write a durable reconciled receipt for each intent. The release adapter must
   atomically recheck the current independent head, pending hold transitions,
   receipt coverage and zero residuals before lifting quarantine. Any uncertainty
   remains HOLD with Selene/Rex custody; hold-policy decisions go to Cora.

## Rehearsal evidence

Use test keys and synthetic workspace/meeting ids. Capture exact source and
migration heads, chain head, zero counts, pending-operation recreation, skipped
cancelled keys and cold-load receipts. Exercise independent DB, DO, playground,
audio object and derived-store restores; a dropped ledger entry; an edited mirror;
a hold after the snapshot; a hold racing a batch; and unavailable adapters.
Do not substitute unit mocks for these acceptance checks.

Rollback removes only the admission RPC. It retains quarantine evidence and
`restore_hold` fences. Source rollback never restores erased content.
